reason: Compared the complete source lem:crossing-test, including the two conclusions after the displayed iff, with SM.crossing_test in SM.Crossings. The theorem takes exactly a concrete tuple P, n>=3 from the inherited source convention, and G1 P. For every remote edge pair i,j it gives IsCrossing P {i,j} iff both source chirotope products equal -1, with all four endpoint indices and determinant orientations matching the source. IsCrossing is independently defined by a finite support equal to the unordered pair {i,j}, remoteness, and nonempty intersection of the actual closed affine segments. Remoteness forces different indices, so a support has exactly two members; it does not encode crossing by the criterion being proved. The Crossing subtype represents these actual unordered supports, without an ordering, root, or additional witness condition. crossingPoint is Classical.choose applied to a proved existence of a common real-plane point. crossingPoint_mem establishes actual segment membership and crossingPoint_unique identifies it with the unique intersection under G1, so it is not an arbitrary encoding of the support or an assumed injective map. The analytic criterion proves that the two strict side products are equivalent to an interior transverse intersection: a nonzero determinant is established before its division is used, and G1 supplies interior membership for geometric remote intersections. The second conjunction is Generic P implying injectivity of crossingPoint on Crossing P, which is exactly distinct crossings having distinct crossing points. Its proof obtains three pairwise-distinct edge indices if two supports differ and then contradicts G2 using their actual common interior point; it does not assume the desired injectivity. The third conjunction asserts finiteness of the actual set of crossing supports, derived from the powerset of the finite modular index set. Proving this already under G1, rather than only under Generic, strengthens the source without dropping any requested case. There are no extra crossing-regularity, oracle, desired-law or literature hypotheses. The source explicitly allows statements on labelled representatives, and the same previously reviewed modular indices and concrete segments are used. This review certifies the complete lemma with those supporting meanings; it does not mark the separate def:crossings row complete while that construction's aggregate and full cyclic-equivariance obligations remain pending. All three conclusions, including the often-overlooked distinct-point and finite-set clauses, are covered. Helper results are not counted as separate original claims.

Mathlib SignType: −1 = neg, neg*neg = pos, pos*neg = neg, zero*_ = zero, so 'product = −1' has the same meaning as the integer product in {−1,0,1}. (ii) Generic P → Function.Injective (@crossingPoint n P): Generic = G1 ∧ G2 (Generic.lean:11-19), G2 = no point in edgeInterior of three pairwise-distinct edges, edgeInterior (Polygon.lean:57-58) = {μ_i + tℓ_i : 0<t<1} = relative interior of a nondegenerate segment (and the single point when ℓ_i = 0, also agreeing), so Generic matches def:generic (lines 111-118).
